🤖 AI-suggested · github-user's review style
The generate action does not import or call report_user_action, so on-demand brief generation events are invisible to product analytics. Without it the Pulse team cannot measure feature adoption or engagement for triggered briefs, which is a key adoption signal. Suggest adding from posthog.event_usage import report_user_action and calling report_user_action(request.user, "pulse brief generated", {...}) with relevant properties like config_id and period_days.

🤖 AI-suggested · Resiliency & SRE Reviewer
start_workflow is called without execution_timeout; if a Temporal server restart re-executes the workflow from a checkpoint between activities, it could run past the implied ~11-minute bound. Add execution_timeout=dt.timedelta(minutes=15) to cap total workflow duration.
As a sanity check, do we also have SLOs for this workflow?

🤖 AI-suggested · Resiliency & SRE Reviewer

Add logger.exception("pulse_brief_dispatch_failed", team_id=self.team_id, brief_id=brief.id) before the bare raise.

🤖 AI-suggested · Architecture & Design Reviewer
Top-level import from ee.hogai.llm import MaxChatOpenAI creates a dependency chain: start_temporal_worker.py → registry.py → activities.py → synthesize.py → ee, all resolved at module-import time. On community edition where ee is not available, importing PULSE_ACTIVITIES/PULSE_WORKFLOWS at worker startup (start_temporal_worker.py lines 202-206) crashes the entire Temporal worker process with ImportError. Invert the coupling: define a BriefSynthesizer protocol in pulse and let an EE module provide the MaxChatOpenAI implementation through a registry or dependency-injection seam.

User-controlled focus_prompt (up to 2000 chars, stored via BriefConfig create/update at products/pulse/backend/api/brief.py:184) is interpolated into an LLM system prompt with only </team_focus> stripped and a <team_focus> fence — the "Ignore that part entirely" instruction is advisory, not enforced (OWASP LLM01 — Prompt Injection). A team member with config write access could craft a focus_prompt that manipulates the LLM into generating fabricated metrics, disregarding the hard rules, or producing policy-violating content in the brief. Sanitize or treat focus_prompt as untrusted data by passing it as a separate non-instruction parameter (e.g., via the LLM provider's structured-context interface) rather than interpolating it into the system prompt.

In api/brief.py line 215, the ProductBrief row is created with status=GENERATING before the try block that connects to Temporal and starts the workflow. If the process crashes between the create and the try (a small window), the brief is stranded in GENERATING with no workflow running. Medium: Pulse writes bypass project RBAC
INTERNAL makes AccessControlPermission skip access-level checks. A read-only project member can therefore create, edit, restore, or delete brief configurations; the same setting on ProductBriefViewSet also lets them trigger billable generation. Use a scope that enforces project write access for mutating actions, or add an explicit permission that distinguishes reads from writes.

Medium: Prompt injection through insight content
item.title and item.description contain user-editable insight names or series labels and are interpolated directly into the system prompt. A project member can add instruction-shaped text to an insight used by an administrator, causing fabricated sections or opportunities to be persisted in the administrator's brief. Sanitize and explicitly frame every user-controlled item field as untrusted data, and validate that generated citations and fingerprint hints refer to the supplied items before persisting the output.
